A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same long-tailed diffusion framework, renamed from CLDM to CCUA. All 20 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original generation experiments, quantitative benchmark results, loss ablations, seed comparisons, and latent-space analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain original DDPM experiments and report new SiT results, batch-resampling experiments, and generated-image comparisons.

M1.justification: The contrastive and timestep-weighted alignment losses and training algorithm remain substantively unchanged under new names. The procedural addition is optional batch resampling, introduced in Section 3.1 and enabled for ImageNet-LT and TinyImageNet-LT. The SiT implementation applies the existing losses to transformer representations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five long-tailed datasets: CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet, and Places, retaining conditional and unconditional generation. CIFAR experiments move to the appendix. ImageNet's changed resolution and backbone alter experimental settings rather than the represented dataset or conditioning task.

E2.justification: The ImageNet comparison changes from DDPM, CBDM, and OCLT in v1 to SiT and SiT with Dispersive Loss in v2. The CIFAR DDPM-1000-step comparison also adds the evaluated omega-scheduler baseline in Table 7. CBDM, OCLT, and ADA remain in corresponding retained DDPM comparisons.

E3.justification: ImageNet changes from 64×64 DDPM trained for 300k iterations to 256×256 SiT evaluated at 40–160 epochs. Sampling changes from DDIM-100 with tuned guidance to ODE-50 with guidance 7.5, and evaluation samples increase from 20k to 50k. v2 adds spatial FID, precision, recall, and batch-resampling settings, including factor 0.1 for ImageNet and TinyImageNet.

E4.justification: v2 Table 5 adds a controlled comparison of SiT and CCUA with and without resampling, testing whether contrastive regularization offsets resampling's diversity loss. New ImageNet and TinyImageNet qualitative comparisons appear. Conversely, v1 Appendix A.4's latent-covariance spectrum analysis disappears. The original loss-component ablation is retained as v2 Table 4.

E5.justification: The CIFAR100-LT comparison using seeds 0, 42, and 2025, its FID values, and the approximately 0.04 versus 0.01 deviation discussion remain unchanged, moving from v1 Table 7 to v2 Table 10. No additional uncertainty estimates or significance tests accompany the new experiments.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the low-resolution ImageNet results with a new SiT result series; at 160 epochs, Table 1 reports FID 19.95 for SiT and 16.41 for CCUA. TinyImageNet's reported FID/FIDtail change from 17.16/37.88 to 15.24/30.39, while head FID changes from 20.39 to 21.32. These replacements involve changed settings, including resampling. Most CIFAR and Places values are retained, with new scheduler and resampling results added.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds mathematical assertions that collapsed embeddings produce loss log N, that this is the maximum loss, and that optimal embeddings are uniform on a hypersphere. These claims have no accompanying proof. The existing contrastive-loss definition and KL-to-MSE derivation remain unchanged apart from notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion broaden applicability from DDPM-focused validation to U-Net and diffusion-transformer architectures, including SiT and 256×256 ImageNet generation. Batch resampling becomes part of the central framework description, and superiority over Dispersive Loss is newly claimed. The explicit claim of being first to adapt conditional-unconditional alignment to diffusion is removed.

C2.justification: v2 explains why resampling supplies more within-tail-class negative pairs and interprets its interaction with CCUA through precision and recall. The dimensional-collapse interpretation from v1 Appendix A.4 is removed, while the central knowledge-sharing explanation remains. The training-cost limitation is extended with a 1.48× SiT overhead alongside the retained 1.6× DDPM overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds explicit U-Net/transformer feature-extraction mappings, four-A6000 SiT hardware, batch size 48, training budgets, and resampling configuration. However, it removes v1's explicit DDPM noise schedule, Adam optimizer, learning rate, and warmup settings, plus CIFAR evaluation sample-count and tail-class details. Reproducibility information is substantially revised in both directions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises the closest-work positioning around Dispersive Loss and REPA: it distinguishes unconditional regularization coupled through alignment from conditional regularization, and direct feature regularization from using an external encoder. SiT and Dhariwal–Nichol are newly cited. The BYOL analogy and explicit first-adaptation assertion disappear; the guidance-scheduler work was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion, and experimental narrative are substantially revised to foreground transformer experiments. CLDM/InfoNCE/MSE terminology becomes CCUA/UCL/AL. CIFAR and unconditional results and limitations move to the appendix, qualitative sections are reorganized, and Appendix B adds a writing-assistance disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening illustration with SiT examples, adds an architecture diagram and ImageNet/TinyImageNet image grids, and introduces SiT and resampling tables. The original combined benchmark table is split across main text and appendix. CIFAR figures are relocated, nearest-neighbor panels are consolidated, and the latent-spectrum figure and several supplementary panels are removed.

improvement.justification: The SiT comparisons, separate fidelity/diversity metrics, and resampling controls strengthen evidence for architectural transfer and help distinguish loss effects from resampling. These gains are partly offset by losing a latent-spectrum diagnostic and explicit optimization details. Moreover, v2 does not reconcile its head-class improvement claim with Table 3's TinyImageNet head FID of 21.32 versus DDPM's 21.27. The evidence supports a positive but limited net improvement.
